meanings: Wendhessa: the pair-name of the archivists of the guild at Eldhythe who took Brenn's words from his mouth and sealed them (IV.3); one name for two, under the lintel, with a dual verb (re rike Wendhessa, re hoska Wendhessa, re sola Wendhessa)
derivation: pair-name by the canon rule (orrowen_v2 §3.10): Wen- (the first post, from his cradle-name) + -dhess- (the second post: her cradle-name without its final vowel, softened as the second element; dh is softened t, or an unchanged dh) + the lintel -a; the cradle-names are not in the Book [wf12 unit S06]

meanings: Tobe: a name (Old Tobe, the fisher of the outpost, IV.3: Tobe hemm)
derivation: *tobeʔa > Hal tobea > tobe (O1,H2), as Aske, Hale; a name: names are names (no sense given) [wf12 unit S06]

meanings: Ebba: a name (Old Ebba of Fenholm, who first said We remember: Ebba hemm)
derivation: *ebb-aʔ > Hal ebbā > ebba (O1,H3), as Bena, Denna (the feminine -a); a name: names are names (no sense given) [wf12 unit S06]

meanings: Wik: a name, the youngest of the runners (the Book's English spells it Wick)
derivation: *wik-o-s > Hal wikos > wik (H2); written k after i at a word's end (orrowen_v2 §2.4), so the Orrowen spelling is Wik where the English keeps Wick; a name: names are names (no sense given) [wf12 unit S06]

meanings: a handle ('hand-place'): the grip of a chest, a tool or a pail; pl. garlowath. IV.3: o yarl um hos garlow, eth ey garl um et ullen, 'his hand on one handle, hers on the other'
derivation: garl 'a hand' + -ow 'place of', as kethow 'a keep' (keth), tevow 'a cradle' (tev) [wf12 unit S06]

meanings: Hold the stone, Seren: the call that opens Seren's own leaves, her word to herself
derivation: a phrase: Keth hold-IMP (to one) + et the + tolm stone (the Invocation's Keth et tolm, canon) + Seren (a name called: s is unchanged by the vocative's softening) [wf12 unit S06]

orrowen: Lymmym galat sa re veskym. Lymmym nayalat ullen.
meanings: What I saw, I carry. I carry nothing else: the runners' oath, sworn with the hand flat on the runners' stone (I.3, IV.3) ('I carry the thing that I saw. I carry nothing other.')
derivation: a phrase: Lymmym carry-1SG (lymm, slender) + galat a thing + sa REL(+S) + re PST(+S) + veskym S·see-1SG (v unchanged) / Lymmym + nayalat nothing (na- + S·galat) + ullen other; the two lines open on the same verb, as the English opens and closes on 'carry' [wf12 unit S06]
logogram: PAR+course (98) + O m · PAR+course (98) + O m
book_lemmas: What I saw, I carry. I carry nothing else.

meanings: Not as Brenn carried: the four words the runners added to their oath, the morning after IV.3 was laid ('not as the carrying of Brenn'); four words in Orrowen as in English
derivation: a phrase: nel is-not (the copula's negative, before a phrase that has no verb) + hosen as + lymmyl carrying (lymm + -Ol, slender -yl) + Wrenn S·Brenn (the possessor softened, b > w, as brodath Wrenn) [wf12 unit S06]
logogram: the turned stone (NOT) · PAR+course (98) + O l

meanings: the runners' stone: the stone a haven's runners swear their oath on, the hand flat upon it ('the stone of the runners'); IV.3: en narl ryss um dholm et haskardath
derivation: a phrase: tolm stone + et the + haskardath runners (haskard + -Ath; a definite possessor: the article, and no mutation), as flenn et tolm [wf12 unit S06]
logogram: TOLM (1) · TRENN+wedge (42) + A r d A th

meanings: mile by mile, every mile ('a mile and a mile')
derivation: a phrase: bost lusul a mile (O0117) + eth and + bost lusul, as fedh eth fedh (O2958) and hos eth hos (O2862); said so because gor 'every' would soften bost to vost, which the tongue hears as another word [wf12 unit S06]

meanings: blot by blot, at every blot ('a blot and a blot'); IV.3: Luth eth luth, re yala Halyna nawrodh, 'At every blot Halyna were silent'
derivation: a phrase: luth ink, stain, blot (O1306, and S06-12) + eth and + luth, as fedh eth fedh (O2958); said so because lo or ul would mutate gor 'every' [wf12 unit S06]

meanings: (new sense of O1306) a blot: the place on a leaf where a name has been cut out, written ▒▒▒▒ (IV.1: Re hadh Rhyna ey nind um et luth; IV.3: luth eth luth)
derivation: new sense of luth 'ink; stain' (O1306): the ink-stain that stands where a name was [wf12 unit S06]

meanings: (new sense of O0614) a letter: a written sheet sent from a post or a hall, the warden's letter (IV.1: flenn hy et deldvar hyvenn sost; IV.3: re hebb ▒▒▒▒ et flenn lom; Re heth et Redul et flenn)
derivation: new sense of flenn 'a leaf of a book or of slate; a sheet' (O0614): a sheet with words on it, sent [wf12 unit S06]

meanings: (new sense of O0994) a seal: the lintel laid across a bundle or a chest, the mark of those who sealed it (IV.3: um hosk havul Wrenn, 'on the seal of Brenn's bundle')
derivation: new sense of hosk 'a lintel; (v.) seal' (O0994): the noun of the sealing [wf12 unit S06]

meanings: (new sense of O0423) (a name, et Derryl) the Harvest: the felling of the black pillars, two generations long (IV.1: um et Derryl; New poduloth sa re hess et Derryl)
derivation: new sense of derryl 'a harvest; reaping' (O0423), as et Ommol 'the Fall' (O1869) [wf12 unit S06]

meanings: (new sense of O1133) (of an answer) a turning aside, a small cleverness: IV.3, Pa vurr surr re nydhym et kylyl lyss ull, 'Forty years have I weighed that small cleverness'
derivation: new sense of kylyl 'a turning' (O1133; kyl 'turn, swerve, hook') [wf12 unit S06]

meanings: It is written: Brenn's answer to the clerk at Eldhythe (IV.3). It answers Ho ross o hosen sy? ('Is it so?') by saying its verb back, which is the tongue's yes, and then says only that the letter says so
derivation: a phrase: Doss is (the state verb) + o it + rytet written (ryt + -At); the yes-by-the-verb of orrowen_v2 §3.4, turned [wf12 unit S06]
a phrase: grem winter + sa REL(+S) + re PST(+S) + orr go (o unchanged): said so because ul would bed grem into an onset the tongue does not allow [wf12 unit S06]

meanings: (new sense of O0222) (v.) thin, grow thin: of mist and the grey (IV.1: Fedh eth fedh re wynt et myst)
derivation: new sense of bynt 'narrow; fine, thin' (O0222): the adjective used as its verb, as lilv 'soft; rot, go soft', lyss 'small; reduce', sell 'long; stretch'; the Thin Sky's word (Helv Bynt, V.4) [wf12 unit S06, fixed after the blind back-translation]
